searched: I read EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 for every Michigan gas and oil plant. Hancock, Livingston and George Johnson are missing from GEM and are adds. The other missing EIA plants have every unit under 50 MW.

I read the MISO queue for Michigan. Request J3922, a 1,445 MW gas combined cycle plant in Branch County, is new to GEM. Two Ottawa County requests at the Roosevelt substation may belong to Zeeland and go to a reviewer.
I read the PJM queue for southwest Michigan. The only gas entry, a 1,120 MW Berrien County request from 2005, was withdrawn.

I worked every power and data center site in the state air permit list that matched no GEM plant. Thomas Township Energy, a 1,250 MW combined cycle plant permitted in 2019 and terminated in 2021, is new to GEM as a cancelled plant. The rest are below the threshold, retired before 2020, never built before 2020, emergency generators, or not generating plants.

I read the Public Service Commission dockets for both big utilities, the Upper Peninsula utilities, Indiana Michigan Power and the data center contracts. Every new gas plant they name is already in GEM.
I read the possible updates sheet for Michigan. The open rows are data centers with diesel backup only, plus the Marshall data center plant that GEM has as MEC North and MEC South.
I checked every Michigan data center announced since 2024. Only the Dowagiac data center plans on-site gas generation, and it goes on the watch list.
irp_summary: Consumers Energy filed its 2026 plan on September 3, 2026 with two new gas plants, at the Karn site in Bay County and at Thetford in Genesee County, both already in GEM, plus a purchase contract with the Midland plant GEM already has.
DTE Electric filed its 2026 plan on September 24, 2026 with about 2.1 GW of new gas in 2031 and 2032, the Milan Township and Handy Township plants already in GEM, which the plant research covers.
Upper Peninsula Power Company's plan in case U-21809 keeps its small Gladstone oil turbine and adds no gas plant.
Upper Michigan Energy Resources' plan in case U-22175 names no new gas plant in the documents I read.
Indiana Michigan Power's plan in case U-22069 adds no gas plant in Michigan.
Northern States Power's plan in case U-21814 covers its Minnesota system and adds no gas plant in Michigan.

qa.recommendation: Decide whether MISO requests J4159 and J4160 are an expansion at Zeeland or a new plant. If no filing ties them to Zeeland by the next batch, add a new plant in Ottawa County from the queue.
qa.note: MISO's generator interconnection queue at https://www.misoenergy.org/planning/resource-utilization/GI_Queue/gi-interactive-queue/ lists two gas requests in Ottawa County, both queued on August 13, 2025 and both connecting at the Roosevelt substation on the METC system. J4159 is a 616 MW combined cycle project in the 2026 study cycle with an in-service date of June 30, 2028. Some copies of the queue, such as the Cleanview list at https://cleanview.co/power-projects/planned/natural-gas-power-plants/michigan, give it as 664 MW, likely the winter rating. J4160 is a 55 MW simple cycle gas turbine with an in-service date of May 31, 2026. The rows are copied at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j4159 and https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j4160. Neither request names a developer. The only gas plants GEM has in Ottawa County are Zeeland generating station and Holland energy park. Neither plant's research for this batch found the requests. I could not find which plant the Roosevelt substation serves. A 55 MW turbine with a 2026 date looks like an addition at an existing plant, and the 616 MW request could be a new combined cycle block there. If it is a new site, the 616 MW request meets the add threshold on the queue entry alone.

qa.recommendation: No add for now. A reviewer may want to confirm that the campus plant is under the 50 MW threshold.
qa.note: EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists EIA plant 50431, University of Michigan, with generators CT6 at 15.5 MW, TG1, TG7 and TG8 at 12.5 MW each, and TG9 and TG10 at 3.5 MW each, all grouped as one combined cycle unit of 60 MW. The state air permit staff report of 2024 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/-5303010553079006113 describes four gas and oil fired boilers feeding steam turbines, plus combined heat and power gas turbines with heat recovery boilers. Most of the steam turbines run on boiler steam, not turbine exhaust, so they are not part of a combined cycle block. The largest gas turbine with its recovery boiler is well under 50 MW. I treated the plant as below the threshold.

monitor.plant_name: Alliance Cloud Services Dowagiac data center gas plant
monitor.monitor_reason: A data center in Dowagiac plans about 40 MW of on-site gas generation. Gas-fired data center plants stay on the watch list until a reviewer promotes them.
monitor.note: A DatacenterDynamics article at https://datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/hyperscale-data-to-expand-michigan-data-center-to-340mw-with-40mw-behind-the-meter-gas-deal says Hyperscale Data plans to grow its Alliance Cloud Services data center in Dowagiac, Michigan to 340 MW. About 40 MW would come from gas generation on site, with gas from SEMCO Energy, and the rest from the grid. The site is 413 East Prairie Ronde Street, Dowagiac, Cass County, state air source B1557, at latitude 41.990967 and longitude -86.100545. Its state air permit to install covers nine 2,000 kW diesel emergency generators. No air permit for gas turbines or engines was found yet. 40 MW is under the 50 MW threshold unless it is an engine or aeroderivative set that grows. Not found: the generator type, maker, number of units and start date.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list the Hancock peaking plant. EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 lists EIA plant 1730, Hancock, owned by DTE Electric Company, in Oakland County. Its Operating sheet rows read: "Hancock | 5 | 41.8 | Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine | 1970" and "Hancock | 6 | 41.8 | Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine | 1966". Generators 1 and 3 are 19 MW each. The point given is latitude 42.5497 and longitude -83.4425. The state air permit staff report at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/3438450417378425065 says the site at 1781 Haggerty Highway in Commerce Township has two Westinghouse combustion turbine generators of 18.5 MW each and two jet turbine generators of 41.27 MW each. The two jet units are Pratt and Whitney FT4 twin pack sets, which are aeroderivative turbines. The report also says one 18.5 MW unit and one 21.5 MW unit were retired on December 22, 2019. The two jet units together make an aeroderivative set of 83.6 MW, which is above the 50 MW threshold, so the plant is an add. The two 19 MW Westinghouse frame units are each under 50 MW and are left out. The staff report says the units were installed between April 1966 and May 1970.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list the Livingston peaking plant near Gaylord. EIA's monthly generator file for September 2026 lists EIA plant 55102, Livingston Generating Station, owned by CMS Generation MI Power LLC, in Otsego County. Its Operating sheet rows read: "Livingston Generating Station | 001 | 42.9 | Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine | 1999" and three more rows for generators 002, 003 and 004 at 42.4 MW each, all from 1999. That is 170.1 MW in all. The point given is latitude 45.030397 and longitude -84.7308. The state air permit staff report dated September 21, 2026 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/-6094188335970412935 covers the site at 155 North Townline Road in Gaylord. It describes four Worthington twin pack natural gas turbine units, each with two engines, rated 39 MW each, with water injection. Twin pack units are aeroderivative sets, so the four units are one set of 170.1 MW, above the 50 MW threshold. CMS Generation Michigan Power LLC is already a GEM owner, entity E100000002589.

newplants.researcher_notes: MISO's generator interconnection queue, read through the data behind its interactive queue page at https://www.misoenergy.org/planning/resource-utilization/GI_Queue/gi-interactive-queue/, lists request J3922 in Branch County, Michigan. It is a gas combined cycle project of 1,445 MW connecting at the Hiple substation on the METC transmission system. It was queued on March 4, 2025, is in the 2025 study cycle, phase 1, with status "Pending Revision Approval", and asks for an in-service date of March 1, 2030. The same row is copied at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/miso-j3922. No developer, plant name, utility filing or air permit names the project. It is not one of the Consumers Energy or DTE Electric gas plants in their 2026 resource plans, which are in Bay, Genesee, Monroe and Livingston counties. The plant is named after its substation and county because the request has no other name. A queue entry is enough to add a plant at announced. Not found: the owner, the turbine model, the exact site and the coordinates.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this proposed plant. The state air permit to install 210-18 at https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/downloadpdf/1162895226898629589 was issued on August 21, 2019 to Thomas Township Energy, LLC for a site east of North Orr Road and north of Geddes Road in Hemlock, Saginaw County. It covers two natural gas combined cycle blocks, each one combustion turbine with a heat recovery boiler and one steam turbine, and each rated at a combined nominal 625 MW. That is 1,250 MW in all. The turbine maker is listed as to be determined. The state permit portal lists the permit as terminated on September 7, 2021, and the site has no other permit or document there. No news story, queue entry or utility filing names the project. GEM tracks cancelled projects from 2020 on, so it is added as cancelled in 2021. The status rests on one source, the state permit record, so it stays at medium confidence. The owner is a project company. The GEM entity system has no entry for Thomas Township Energy LLC, so it would be a new entity.
newplants.action: Create the plant in Hemlock, Saginaw County, Michigan, then add the two units below as cancelled, cancellation year 2021, with no start year. Add Thomas Township Energy LLC as a new owner entity.
